text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like this, KWEB returned a median of 0.68% over the following 10 sessions, with a wide spread from -9.23% to 43.14%. The single number to anchor on for path risk is the median max adverse excursion of -3.3%, which shows that even when the endpoint was positive, the intra-horizon drawdown was frequently uncomfortable. This is a description of a historical conditional distribution, not a forecast of what KWEB will do next.

[state]
The engine retrieved these specific analogs because the current state of KWEB as of 2026-09-18 is defined by three extreme features. First, the distance from 52-week high (dist52) is -42.74%, carrying a z-score of -1.899, meaning the ETF is deeply off its highs relative to its own history. Second, the 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) is -2.663 in raw terms, mapped to a used z-score of -1.607, indicating severely depressed liquidity. Third, WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) is 19.24%, a z-score of 1.124, introducing an unusual macro backdrop. These features dominate the name group, which carries a 30% weight in the distance metric. The retrieval pulled 50 analogs across 35 distinct sessions and 28 distinct symbols, with only 4 being KWEB itself. The closest match was 0.3408 in distance, and the median distance was 0.4827. The sector breakdown leans heavily into Technology (14), China ADR (7), Health Care (7), Consumer Disc. (6), and ETF China (5).

[history]
Over the 10-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a mean return of 1.81% and a median of 0.68%, but the standard deviation was 8.19%, and the skew was 2.601, driven entirely by one massive outlier. The 10th percentile was -5.81% and the 90th percentile was 8.66%. In 56% of the analogs the return was above zero; in 44% it was below. The bad tail is populated by recent weakness: NKE on 2026-09-03 returned -8.41%, PDD on 2026-08-31 returned -7.05%, NKE on 2026-08-13 returned -6.77%, HD on 2026-09-03 returned -5.69%, and KWEB itself on 2026-08-31 returned -5.15%. The good tail is dominated by a single NIO session on 2025-07-08 that returned 43.14%. Without that NIO observation, the right tail collapses. The histogram confirms this: 18% of outcomes clustered near 0.59%, while the 42.05% midpoint bin holds just 2% of the mass, representing that lone NIO spike.

[tails]
A position can end near flat and still be un-holdable. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -3.3%. The 25th percentile of adverse excursion was -5.96%, and the 10th percentile was -7.26%. On the upside, the median max favourable excursion was 4.04%, the 75th percentile was 8.43%, and the 90th percentile was 14.31%, yielding a reward-risk ratio of 1.22. Looking at specific drawdown thresholds during the 10 sessions, the probability of breaching a 5% drawdown was 32 out of 50 episodes. The probability of breaching a 10% drawdown was 2 out of 50. No analog breached a 15% or 20% drawdown threshold. The conformal interval, scaled to target 80% coverage, spans from -11.54% to 12.9%, a total width of 24.44%.

[stress]
The stress scenarios reveal how this setup behaves under specific regimes. The 2020-02/03 liquidity crash scenario is the most severe: using 48 analogs, the median forward return was -9.75%, a delta of -10.43% versus the baseline, with a 10th percentile of -23.23% and a 75% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one. The 2025-04 tariff shock scenario, directly relevant to China exposure, used 26 analogs and produced a median of -3.36% (delta -4.04%), a 10th percentile of -17.57%, and a 65.4% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown. Its caveat is that policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario used 50 analogs for a median of -4.81% (delta -5.49%) and a 30% probability of breaching a 10% drawdown; its caveat is that a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly, so treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind showed a median of -2.77% (delta -3.45%) and a 22.2% breach probability; its caveat is that the reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. Conversely, the 2023-03 regional bank stress scenario actually improved the median to 4.4% (delta +3.72%) with a 0% breach probability, but its caveat is that it is a very short window dominated by a handful of sessions. Shock-based scenarios like Volatility spike (+2 sigma VIX), Policy-rate path re-pricing (+1.5 sigma), Liquidity air pocket, Earnings release day, FOMC decision day, Crypto drawdown contagion, and China ADR de-rating all produced medians between -1.25% and 0.78%, with deltas ranging from -1.93% to +0.1%. Their respective caveats note that VIX shocks mean-revert quickly; rate proxies ignore name-level duration; gap20 measures the underlying exchange, not a 7x24 venue; earnings dates for foreign issuers are noisier than domestic ones; only 92 FOMC days exist making the set small and overlapping; BTC is a market-wide proxy without identified name-level linkage; and delisting risks are structural and invisible to price/vol features. No scenarios were skipped.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." Specifically, the directional hit rate is 49.8%, and the matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -2.4%. The PIT chi-square is 306.6 against a critical value of 16.92. The dataset spans 2513 sessions from 2016-09-20 to 2026-09-18 across 71 symbols. Regarding the wrapper layer, the status is no-verified-wrapper. No Gate.io spot v4 listing passed both verification tests against KWEB, so no wrapper figure is reported for it and none is estimated. The reference market calendar shows that the cash market is closed for 81.4% of the week (136.67 hours out of 168), but because there is no verified tokenised wrapper, there is no closed-session return distribution behind this measurement on this build. Do not substitute figures from another instrument.
